chunk_findings.detail: The contract declares `ddflow.core.digest` as the one owner of hashlib — its name says so, its comment says "Content digests live in ddflow.core.digest" (present tense, unlike the extras contract whose comment explicitly says a *future* task adds the entry), and this change's own guard rule is "hashlib outside core.digest". Yet the `ignore_imports` list enumerates 18 other modules and omits the home itself: `ddflow.core.digest -> hashlib` is absent. Since `source_modules = ddflow` and `allow_indirect_imports = True`, the home module's own `import hashlib` (which is the whole reason the module is named in the contract) is a reported violation with no matching ignore entry, so `lint-imports` exits non-zero, `tests/test_architecture_guards.py` fails, and the pre-push hook this change wires up is red on the first push. This directly contradicts the file header's promise that `ignore_imports` "lists the imports that break the rule TODAY" so that "the contract passes today". Demonstrated input: `ddflow/core/digest.py` containing `import hashlib` → violation "ddflow.core.digest is not allowed to import hashlib", no ignore entry matches. Fix: add `ddflow.core.digest -> hashlib` (and mark it `# home`, as `subprocess-home` does for `ddflow.infra.proc`).

chunk_findings.detail: Same defect: the contract (and its comment "Atomic writes, temporary files and locks live in ddflow.infra.fsio", plus the change description's rule "write_text/tempfile/os.replace outside infra.fsio") makes `ddflow.infra.fsio` the sole owner of tempfile/fcntl, but the allowlist lists 15 non-home importers and never `ddflow.infra.fsio -> tempfile` / `ddflow.infra.fsio -> fcntl`. A module that owns `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile` / `fcntl.flock` inevitably imports both, so `lint-imports` reports two unignored violations from the home module and the contract cannot pass; the ratchet starts broken rather than "passing today". Demonstrated input: `ddflow/infra/fsio.py` with `import tempfile` and `import fcntl` → two violations, neither ignored. Fix: add the two home entries (or, if the module genuinely does not exist yet, say so the way `subprocess-home` hedges `ddflow.infra.git` with "when it exists" — as written, the present-tense comment asserts it exists).

chunk_findings.detail:
The import-linter check pipes the return value of `lint_imports` straight into `sys.exit`:

```python
"import sys; from importlinter.cli import lint_imports; "
"sys.exit(lint_imports(config_filename='.importlinter', no_cache=True, no_logo=True))",
...
assert proc.returncode == 0, (...)
```

`importlinter.cli.lint_imports` returns a `bool` whose documented meaning is "`True` if the contracts were kept" (its own CLI entry point does `sys.exit(0 if passed else 1)`). Because `True` is an `int` with value `1`, `sys.exit(True)` terminates the child with status **1**, and `sys.exit(False)` terminates with status **0**. So the exit status is exactly inverted relative to the assertion:

- Healthy repo (all `.importlinter` contracts kept, which the change's intent says is the state "today"): `lint_imports` returns `True` → child exits `1` → `proc.returncode == 0` is false → **`test_import_contracts` fails on a correct tree**.
- Broken contract (a forbidden import added, or a stale `ignore_imports` entry with `unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = error`): `lint_imports` returns `False` → child exits `0` → the assert **passes silently**, so a real architecture regression is not caught.

The fix is to normalize the bool before exiting (e.g. `sys.exit(0 if lint_imports(...) else 1)`). Note this also means the guard never actually enforces the layer/forbidden-import contracts it was written for: it rejects valid code and green-lights the violations it is supposed to ratchet down.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_guards.py :: test_import_contracts

chunk_findings.detail: This change locks a new binary crypto dependency, `cryptography 50.0.2`, into `uv.lock`, but nothing in the stated intent authorizes it: the change is described as dev-only tooling (`hypothesis`, `syrupy`, `import-linter`, `mutmut`, `networkx`, `markdown-it-py`) plus the `[search]`/`[watch]`/`[rag]`/`[mcp-sdk]` extras, none of which pulls in `cryptography` (nor its `cffi` dep). The entry is inserted in sorted position (between `colorama` and `ddflow-mcp`), so it is a first/only definition, and this file's single hunk touches only `colorama`→`ddflow-mcp`; no hunk in this patch adds `cffi`. Concretely, on the pre-push stage running `uv sync --frozen` (or `uv lock --check`) in an environment whose `pyproject.toml` does not declare `cryptography`, either the lock resolves a package that is not in the project's dependency graph (lockfile out of date / silently pruned on the next `uv lock`, meaning the committed lock no longer reproduces what CI builds) or, because `cryptography` declares `cffi` as a dependency and no `cffi` package entry is added by this patch, resolution fails with `cffi is not present in the lockfile`. Either way the guard this series is adding does not pass with the committed lockfile, and a native-code crypto library has been introduced as an undeclared dependency.
chunk_findings.title: uv.lock (new `[[package]] name = "cryptography"` entry, added at ~line 181)

chunk_findings.detail: The change's stated dev-only dependency set is "hypothesis, syrupy, import-linter, mutmut, networkx and markdown-it-py", but this lock update adds only `import-linter` (plus `pylint` and `radon`) to the root package's `dev` group; `hypothesis`, `syrupy`, `mutmut`, `networkx` and `markdown-it-py` do not appear anywhere in the root `dev = [...]` list. Because the `dev` list is fully visible in this hunk (context line `dev = [` … context lines `pytest`/`pytest-timeout`/`pytest-xdist`/`ruff` … context ` ]`), this is not a truncation artifact of the split diff: the lock's project dev-dependencies genuinely omit those five. Consequence: if pyproject declares them as dev dependencies (as the change states), `uv lock --check` / `uv sync --frozen` in the pre-push stage fails with a lockfile-out-of-date error before any guard runs; if pyproject does not declare them, the tests introduced by this change that import them raise `ModuleNotFoundError` in CI. Either way the recorded dev environment does not match the change's own dependency list, and the fix is to regenerate `uv.lock` (or add the five entries and their transitive packages).
chunk_findings.title: uv.lock `[package.dev-dependencies]` / `[package.metadata.requires-dev]` (dev list)

chunk_findings.detail: This lockfile hunk adds two package names that are near-identical to, and phonetically confusable with, packages added in the same hunk (`httpx` 0.28.1, `httpcore` 1.0.9), plus a `httpx2-jsfetch` helper for an emscripten fetch backend. Every other package in this hunk is a legitimate closure of a declared dependency: `filelock/fsspec/hf-xet/huggingface-hub/httpx/httpcore/h11/idna` hang off `huggingface-hub` (the `[rag]` model2vec oracle), and `grimp` hangs off `import-linter`, whose other deps (`click`, `rich`, `typing-extensions`) already exist. Nothing in the diff declares a dependency on `httpx2`, `httpcore2`, or `httpx2-jsfetch`: `huggingface-hub` depends on `httpx`/`httpcore`, and `httpx` depends on `httpcore`, so the `*2` entries are unreachable from the resolved graph. A uv lock cannot legitimately contain packages with no dependents, so either the lock is inconsistent (`uv sync --frozen` / `uv lock --check` will fail with a stale/out-of-date lock, because `httpx2`/`httpcore2` pull `truststore`, which is not defined anywhere in this hunk) or, if some manifest outside this diff does reference them, `uv sync` will install a typosquat lookalike of `httpx`/`httpcore` into the dev environment. Either way the entries should not be committed; if the intent was an HTTP client for the `[mcp-sdk]`/`[rag]` adapter, the correct spec is the already-present `httpx`.
chunk_findings.title: uv.lock (added `httpx2` 2.13.1, `httpcore2` 2.13.1, `httpx2-jsfetch` 1.0)

chunk_findings.detail: The added `mcp` 2.3.0 lock entry declares a hard dependency `{ name = "httpx2" }`. No such distribution exists (the real dependency is `httpx`, with `httpx-sse` for SSE). Since this lockfile addition is pulled in unconditionally by the `[mcp-sdk]` extra, `uv lock --check` / `uv sync --locked` in the pre-push stage will fail to resolve `httpx2`, breaking the pipeline for all developers rather than only when the extra is exercised. Either the name is a typo for `httpx`/`httpx-sse`, or the entry was hand-edited and does not match what `uv lock` would generate.
chunk_findings.title: uv.lock (new `mcp` 2.3.0 package `dependencies` list)

chunk_findings.detail: The change description states the current, ratcheted-down-from numbers as "in-function imports (570), radon grade D+ functions (104)", but the committed `BASELINE` sets those two entries to 621 and 112. `test_ratchet` asserts both directions (`count <= baseline` and `count >= baseline`), so if the counters produce the counts the description says exist today, the second assertion fires for both kinds: `deferred_imports: 570 sites, below the baseline of 621 ... now lower it` and `complexity_d_or_worse: 104 sites, below the baseline of 112`, i.e. the guard fails on every run of the pre-push stage it was added to (I verified the deferred-import counter is faithful to its definition — every `Import`/`ImportFrom` at `depth > 0`, with `depth` symmetrically incremented only by `FunctionDef`/`AsyncFunctionDef`/`Lambda` — so it cannot be producing an inflated 621 for a repo with 570 in-function imports). Setting a baseline *above* the live count is also precisely the failure mode the module docstring forbids ("nothing can quietly grow back into the room it left"): the 621/112 entries leave headroom for 51 new in-function imports and 8 new grade-D+ functions to be added before `count <= baseline` would complain.

chunk_findings.detail: The root project's dev group in the regenerated lock lists only `import-linter`, `pylint`, `pytest`, `pytest-timeout`, `pytest-xdist`, `radon`, `ruff`, but the change declares the dev-only dependency set as `hypothesis`, `syrupy`, `import-linter`, `mutmut`, `networkx` and `markdown-it-py` (plus `pylint`/`radon` used by the ratchet test). Five of the declared dev deps (`hypothesis`, `syrupy`, `mutmut`, `networkx`, `markdown-it-py`) are referenced nowhere in the lock: they are neither in the `dev` group nor in `[package.metadata.requires-dev] dev`. Concretely, running `uv lock --check` against the pyproject that declares those deps fails with "lock is out of date", and even if the lock is accepted, `uv sync --dev` installs only the seven listed entries — so the pre-push guard test that imports the networkx / markdown-it-py oracles or the syrupy-based baseline snapshots dies with `ModuleNotFoundError` instead of reporting the ratchet counts. Either the lock must be regenerated to include those five dev deps, or the declaration of them must be dropped from the change; as committed, the lock and the declared environment disagree.

chunk_findings.detail: `_parse_duplicates` now treats pylint exit bit 2 (an error-category message was emitted) as "pylint could not run", but that is not what bit 2 means. Bits 1 (fatal) and 32 (usage) are the cases where pylint genuinely failed to produce a report; bit 2 is just `ERROR` in the same category mask as 4/8/16, which the docstring itself documents as "only say which message categories were emitted". Pylint continues analysing and still emits every `R0801` needed for the ratchet when it emits an `E…` message, so rejecting bit 2 only turns reproducible, correctly measured runs into failures. Concrete case: the change set itself ships optional extras (`rapidfuzz`, `watchfiles`, `model2vec`, `sqlite-vec`, the MCP SDK) that are imported in exactly one adapter each, and the pre-push/dev environment installs only the dev deps, not those extras. With the `[search]` extra absent, pylint emits `E0401: Unable to import 'rapidfuzz'` for that one adapter, exits with `2 | 8` (error + refactor), and this assert raises `AssertionError: pylint could not run (exit 10)` instead of comparing the cluster count with the baseline. Before this hunk the same run passed (`returncode & 32` is 0) and the duplicate-code ratchet worked, so the error-message bit is not needed to protect against the empty-output-reads-as-zero problem the docstring describes — 1 and 32 alone do that.

chunk_findings.detail: The contract declares `ddflow.core.digest` as the one owner of hashlib — its name says so, its comment says "Content digests live in ddflow.core.digest" (present tense, unlike the extras contract whose comment explicitly says a *future* task adds the entry), and this change's own guard rule is "hashlib outside core.digest". Yet the `ignore_imports` list enumerates 18 other modules and omits the home itself: `ddflow.core.digest -> hashlib` is absent. Since `source_modules = ddflow` and `allow_indirect_imports = True`, the home module's own `import hashlib` (which is the whole reason the module is named in the contract) is a reported violation with no matching ignore entry, so `lint-imports` exits non-zero, `tests/test_architecture_guards.py` fails, and the pre-push hook this change wires up is red on the first push. This directly contradicts the file header's promise that `ignore_imports` "lists the imports that break the rule TODAY" so that "the contract passes today". Demonstrated input: `ddflow/core/digest.py` containing `import hashlib` → violation "ddflow.core.digest is not allowed to import hashlib", no ignore entry matches. Fix: add `ddflow.core.digest -> hashlib` (and mark it `# home`, as `subprocess-home` does for `ddflow.infra.proc`).

chunk_findings.detail:
The import-linter check pipes the return value of `lint_imports` straight into `sys.exit`:

```python
"import sys; from importlinter.cli import lint_imports; "
"sys.exit(lint_imports(config_filename='.importlinter', no_cache=True, no_logo=True))",
...
assert proc.returncode == 0, (...)
```

`importlinter.cli.lint_imports` returns a `bool` whose documented meaning is "`True` if the contracts were kept" (its own CLI entry point does `sys.exit(0 if passed else 1)`). Because `True` is an `int` with value `1`, `sys.exit(True)` terminates the child with status **1**, and `sys.exit(False)` terminates with status **0**. So the exit status is exactly inverted relative to the assertion:

- Healthy repo (all `.importlinter` contracts kept, which the change's intent says is the state "today"): `lint_imports` returns `True` → child exits `1` → `proc.returncode == 0` is false → **`test_import_contracts` fails on a correct tree**.
- Broken contract (a forbidden import added, or a stale `ignore_imports` entry with `unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting = error`): `lint_imports` returns `False` → child exits `0` → the assert **passes silently**, so a real architecture regression is not caught.

The fix is to normalize the bool before exiting (e.g. `sys.exit(0 if lint_imports(...) else 1)`). Note this also means the guard never actually enforces the layer/forbidden-import contracts it was written for: it rejects valid code and green-lights the violations it is supposed to ratchet down.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_guards.py :: test_import_contracts

chunk_findings.detail: This change locks a new binary crypto dependency, `cryptography 50.0.2`, into `uv.lock`, but nothing in the stated intent authorizes it: the change is described as dev-only tooling (`hypothesis`, `syrupy`, `import-linter`, `mutmut`, `networkx`, `markdown-it-py`) plus the `[search]`/`[watch]`/`[rag]`/`[mcp-sdk]` extras, none of which pulls in `cryptography` (nor its `cffi` dep). The entry is inserted in sorted position (between `colorama` and `ddflow-mcp`), so it is a first/only definition, and this file's single hunk touches only `colorama`→`ddflow-mcp`; no hunk in this patch adds `cffi`. Concretely, on the pre-push stage running `uv sync --frozen` (or `uv lock --check`) in an environment whose `pyproject.toml` does not declare `cryptography`, either the lock resolves a package that is not in the project's dependency graph (lockfile out of date / silently pruned on the next `uv lock`, meaning the committed lock no longer reproduces what CI builds) or, because `cryptography` declares `cffi` as a dependency and no `cffi` package entry is added by this patch, resolution fails with `cffi is not present in the lockfile`. Either way the guard this series is adding does not pass with the committed lockfile, and a native-code crypto library has been introduced as an undeclared dependency.
chunk_findings.title: uv.lock (new `[[package]] name = "cryptography"` entry, added at ~line 181)

chunk_findings.detail: The change's stated dev-only dependency set is "hypothesis, syrupy, import-linter, mutmut, networkx and markdown-it-py", but this lock update adds only `import-linter` (plus `pylint` and `radon`) to the root package's `dev` group; `hypothesis`, `syrupy`, `mutmut`, `networkx` and `markdown-it-py` do not appear anywhere in the root `dev = [...]` list. Because the `dev` list is fully visible in this hunk (context line `dev = [` … context lines `pytest`/`pytest-timeout`/`pytest-xdist`/`ruff` … context ` ]`), this is not a truncation artifact of the split diff: the lock's project dev-dependencies genuinely omit those five. Consequence: if pyproject declares them as dev dependencies (as the change states), `uv lock --check` / `uv sync --frozen` in the pre-push stage fails with a lockfile-out-of-date error before any guard runs; if pyproject does not declare them, the tests introduced by this change that import them raise `ModuleNotFoundError` in CI. Either way the recorded dev environment does not match the change's own dependency list, and the fix is to regenerate `uv.lock` (or add the five entries and their transitive packages).
chunk_findings.title: uv.lock `[package.dev-dependencies]` / `[package.metadata.requires-dev]` (dev list)

chunk_findings.detail: This lockfile hunk adds two package names that are near-identical to, and phonetically confusable with, packages added in the same hunk (`httpx` 0.28.1, `httpcore` 1.0.9), plus a `httpx2-jsfetch` helper for an emscripten fetch backend. Every other package in this hunk is a legitimate closure of a declared dependency: `filelock/fsspec/hf-xet/huggingface-hub/httpx/httpcore/h11/idna` hang off `huggingface-hub` (the `[rag]` model2vec oracle), and `grimp` hangs off `import-linter`, whose other deps (`click`, `rich`, `typing-extensions`) already exist. Nothing in the diff declares a dependency on `httpx2`, `httpcore2`, or `httpx2-jsfetch`: `huggingface-hub` depends on `httpx`/`httpcore`, and `httpx` depends on `httpcore`, so the `*2` entries are unreachable from the resolved graph. A uv lock cannot legitimately contain packages with no dependents, so either the lock is inconsistent (`uv sync --frozen` / `uv lock --check` will fail with a stale/out-of-date lock, because `httpx2`/`httpcore2` pull `truststore`, which is not defined anywhere in this hunk) or, if some manifest outside this diff does reference them, `uv sync` will install a typosquat lookalike of `httpx`/`httpcore` into the dev environment. Either way the entries should not be committed; if the intent was an HTTP client for the `[mcp-sdk]`/`[rag]` adapter, the correct spec is the already-present `httpx`.
chunk_findings.title: uv.lock (added `httpx2` 2.13.1, `httpcore2` 2.13.1, `httpx2-jsfetch` 1.0)

chunk_findings.detail: The added `mcp` 2.3.0 lock entry declares a hard dependency `{ name = "httpx2" }`. No such distribution exists (the real dependency is `httpx`, with `httpx-sse` for SSE). Since this lockfile addition is pulled in unconditionally by the `[mcp-sdk]` extra, `uv lock --check` / `uv sync --locked` in the pre-push stage will fail to resolve `httpx2`, breaking the pipeline for all developers rather than only when the extra is exercised. Either the name is a typo for `httpx`/`httpx-sse`, or the entry was hand-edited and does not match what `uv lock` would generate.
chunk_findings.title: uv.lock (new `mcp` 2.3.0 package `dependencies` list)

chunk_findings.detail: The new abort condition `assert not returncode & (1 | 2 | 32)` classifies bit 2 as "pylint could not run", but bit 2 is set by any **error-category (E) message having been emitted** — exactly the same kind of signal as bits 4/8/16 for W/R/C messages. The docstring's own split ("4, 8 and 16 only say which message categories were emitted") applies to bit 2 as well; only bit 1 (fatal) and bit 32 (usage error) indicate the tool itself failed. Concrete input: run pylint with its default checker set over a tree whose adapter module imports an optional extra that is not installed in the dev environment (`import rapidfuzz`, or `import watchfiles`/`model2vec`). pylint prints `E0401: Unable to import 'rapidfuzz'` and exits with `2`, *while still printing the complete R0801 duplicate report*, so the cluster count is measured and comparable to the baseline. `_parse_duplicates` now raises `AssertionError: pylint could not run (exit 2)` and the ratchet fails for a run that measured everything; the same run passed under the old `& 32` check. The mask should be `1 | 32` (or left at `32`) if only runs that genuinely produced no measurement are to abort.
